props.gloss_en: one who was standing in prayer and water ran on his knees stops until the water ceases, and resumes praying
he returns to the beginning [of the prayer]
he returns to the place where he stopped
entertained: their dispute turns on one who delayed long enough to finish the whole prayer
entertained: on the second master's view, even one who delayed that long returns to where he stopped
Rav Ashi, against the proposal: this 'if he delayed' -- it is 'if he did not delay' that needed saying
Rav Ashi: all agree that one who delayed long enough to finish the whole of it returns to the beginning
Rav Ashi: and there they dispute one who did not delay that long
one master holds he is a disqualified man, not fit, and his prayer is no prayer [so he returns to the beginning]
the other holds he is a fit man and his prayer is a prayer [so he returns to where he stopped]
one who needs to relieve himself may not pray
and if he prayed, his prayer is an abomination
they taught this only where he cannot hold himself back
but if he can hold himself back, his prayer is a prayer
and for how long [must he be able to hold himself]? up to a parasang
R' Yonatan: one who needs to relieve himself may not pray
R' Yonatan's source: 'prepare to meet your God, O Israel' (Amos 4:12)
R' Yonatan: 'guard your foot when you go to the house of God' (Eccl 4:17) -- guard yourself not to sin, and if you sin, bring an offering before Me
Rava: 'and draw near to listen' -- be near to hear the words of the wise, who when they sin bring an offering and repent
[Rava, continuing:] 'than the fools' giving a sacrifice' -- do not be like the fools, who sin and bring an offering and do not repent
entertained: 'for they know not to do evil' means what it says -- they do not know how to do evil
if so, they are righteous!

rather: do not be like the fools who sin and bring an offering and do not know whether they bring it for the good or for the evil; the Holy One said: they cannot tell good from evil, and they bring an offering before Me?!
Rav Ashi: ['guard your foot' means] guard your orifices when you stand in prayer before Me
one who enters a privy removes his tefillin at a distance of four cubits, and enters
Rav Sheshet: they taught this only of a fixed privy
but in a makeshift privy he removes them and relieves himself at once
and when he leaves [the makeshift privy], he distances four cubits and puts them on
because he has made it a fixed privy
Ravina: one may enter a fixed privy in tefillin to urinate
it is forbidden to enter a fixed privy in tefillin to urinate (Rav Adda bar Mattana; Rava's answer)
Rava's reason: we are concerned lest he defecate in them
Rava's reason in the other version: lest he break wind in them
Beit Shammai: [entering a fixed privy] he removes them at four cubits, puts them in the window next to the public domain and enters; leaving, he distances four cubits and puts them on
Beit Hillel: he holds them in his hand and enters
R' Akiva [as the baraita reads]: he holds them in his garment and enters
sometimes he forgets them and they fall
rather read [R' Akiva]: he holds them in his garment and in his hand and enters
and he puts them in the holes next to the privy
and he does not put them in the holes next to the public domain
lest passers-by take them and he come under suspicion

the incident: a student left his tefillin in the holes next to the public domain; a harlot took them, came to the study-hall and said 'see what so-and-so gave me as my fee'; hearing it, the student went up to the roof, fell and died
at that hour they enacted that he hold them in his garment and in his hand and enter
at first they would put tefillin in the holes next to the privy, and mice would come and take them
they enacted that they be put in the windows next to the public domain [because of the mice]
passers-by would come and take them; they enacted that he hold them in his hand and enter
R' Meyasha: the halakha -- he rolls them up like a scroll and holds them in his right hand against his heart
Rav Nachman: provided no strap hangs out below his hand a handbreadth
R' Zeira: they taught [rolling them like a scroll] only where there is still time in the day to put them on
but where there is no time left in the day to put them on, he makes them a pouch of a handbreadth and puts them in it
R' Yochanan: by day he rolls them like a scroll and holds them in his hand against his heart
and by night he makes them a pouch of a handbreadth and puts them in it
Abaye: they taught [a handbreadth pouch] only of a vessel that is their own vessel
but in a vessel that is not their own vessel -- even less than a handbreadth
Mar Zutra: know it -- small flasks protect [their contents] in a tent over a corpse
R' Yochanan, about to enter the privy, would hand his companions a book of aggada he was holding, but not tefillin
since the Rabbis permitted them [to be held in the privy], they will guard me
Rav Nachman would likewise hand over a book of aggada he was holding, but not tefillin
one may not hold tefillin in his hand and a Torah scroll in his arm and pray
nor urinate in them
nor sleep in them, neither fixed sleep nor casual sleep
Shmuel: a knife, coins, a bowl and a loaf are like them (Steinsaltz: as to praying while holding them)
Rav Sheshet: the halakha is not as this baraita [not to urinate in them], for it is Beit Shammai's
the baraita: things I permitted you here, I forbade you there
the stam's answer: that baraita was taught of [uncovering] a handbreadth and two, not of tefillin
one baraita: when relieving himself, he uncovers a handbreadth behind and two in front
another baraita: a handbreadth behind and nothing in front
entertained: both speak of a man -- the two-handbreadth baraita of urination
entertained: and the nothing-in-front baraita of defecation
if [it spoke] of urination, why would he need [to uncover] a handbreadth behind?
rather both speak of defecation: the two-handbreadth baraita of a man
and the nothing-in-front baraita of a woman
the baraita, on its 'permitted here, forbidden there': this is a kal vachomer that has no refutation
rather, is it not [about] tefillin -- permitted in the fixed privy, forbidden in the makeshift one
a fixed privy, where there are no splashes, [Beit Hillel] permit; a makeshift one, where there are splashes, they forbid
the baraita means: derive this matter by way of reason, not by kal vachomer -- for were it derived by kal vachomer, it would be a kal vachomer that has no refutation

schemas.gloss_en: דאי בית הלל: השתא בית הכסא קבוע שרי, בית הכסא עראי מיבעיא?! -- on Beit Hillel's view holding tefillin is permitted in a fixed privy, so a fortiori in a makeshift one; hence a baraita forbidding urinating in them cannot be Beit Hillel's, and must be Beit Shammai's (Rav Sheshet's ground for p_leit_hilchta_bs). Re-raised by the stam after the teyuvta: מכל מקום קשיא (23b.10)

grounds.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: בית הכסא קבוע דליכא ניצוצות שרו, בית הכסא עראי דאיכא ניצוצות אסרי -- the makeshift privy has splashes, which the fixed one does not (= p_nitzotzot)

supports.gloss_en: תדע, שהרי פכין קטנים מצילין באהל המת -- small flasks protect in a corpse-tent, so a vessel under a handbreadth still counts (Steinsaltz: though a handbreadth is otherwise the minimum barrier)

challenges.gloss_en: אלא לאו תפילין, ותיובתא דרבא אמר רב ששת. תיובתא

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: דברים שהתרתי לך כאן אסרתי לך כאן -- מאי לאו תפילין? per Beit Hillel: permitted in the fixed privy, forbidden in the makeshift one; per Beit Shammai nothing was permitted at all. Answered at 23b.5 (the baraita concerns a handbreadth and two), but the answer is dropped at 23b.9 (אלא לאו תפילין)
אי הכי, הא דקתני עלה זהו קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה -- מאי אין עליו תשובה? דרכא דמלתא הכי איתא: man and woman simply differ, so there is no kal vachomer here to call unrefuted
אי הכי, אמאי אין עליו תשובה? תשובה מעלייתא היא! -- the splashes are an excellent refutation

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: derive it by way of reason, not by kal vachomer; were it derived by kal vachomer, it would be one without refutation (= p_betorat_taama)
